title: Fix the employment types
prompt: Payroll needs every employment type as `full_time`, `part_time` or `contractor`. The function below leaves short forms like ` FT` unmapped and turns `Full  Time` into `full__time`. Fix `solve(employees)`.
rules: Standardize `employment_type`: no spaces at the start or end, all lower case, and each run of spaces or hyphens between words becomes one underscore.
After that, the short forms `ft`, `pt` and `contract` become `full_time`, `part_time` and `contractor`. Other values stay as they are.
A missing type stays missing. Return `employee_id` and `employment_type`, one row per employee.
hints: Feed the starter ` FT` in your head: `replace` runs first, on the raw value, and ` FT` isn't exactly `ft`.
`replace` matches whole values, so standardize first and map afterwards, on the tidied column.
`[ -]` matches one character at a time, so two spaces become two underscores. Add `+` to match a whole run.
explanation: Two bugs. `replace` matches whole values, and the starter runs it on the raw column, so ` FT` or `Contract` never equals a key in the dict; standardize first, then map. And `[ -]` matches a single character, so a run of two spaces becomes two underscores; `[ -]+` (or `[\\s-]+`) turns each run into one. The fixed version: `tidy = F.regexp_replace(F.lower(F.trim("employment_type")), "[ -]+", "_")`, then `employees.select("employee_id", tidy.alias("employment_type")).replace({"ft": "full_time", "pt": "part_time", "contract": "contractor"}, subset=["employment_type"])`. The `replace` now sees `ft`, `pt` and `contract` exactly, and leaves `full_time` and anything else alone.
